newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra wants environmental study from Chevron.
newsitem.headline: Canberra wants environmental study from Chevron.

text.p: The Australian government on Monday said it would require Chevron Corp to produce an environmental impact statement for its proposed natural-gas pipeline from Papua New Guinea into northeast Australia.
Chevron would have to meet high standards, Environment Minister Robert Hill said in a statement.

"The Commonwealth (federal) government is committed to ensuring that the environmental-impact-assessment process is rigorous, transparent and efficient," Hill said. "We expect proponents to meet high standards of environmental protection."

But Resources Minister Warwick Parer promised to cut red tape for Chevron and Comalco Ltd, which is studying the parallel development of an alumina refinery in Gladstone, Queensland, to use gas from the pipeline.
"I fully commit the services of my department's New Project Facilitation Branch to cut through red tape and remove roadblocks," Parer said in a statement.
Hill said Australia would cut the burden of the environmental impact statement by combining the federal and Queensland state processes.
"Draft guidelines (for the study) are expected to be available later this month," he said.
"When the guidelines are finalised, Chevron will prepare a draft (environmental impact statement) which will be released for public review," Hill said.
That statement would have to address all significant environmental issues. Comalco is 67 percent owned by Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd.
